name: Latvia
tagline: The largest collection of Art Nouveau in Europe, on the edge of a great pine forest.
summary: Latvia's capital was one of the Baltic's richest ports in 1900, and it spent the money on facades — whole streets of them, with faces and peacocks and screaming stone masks. Outside Riga the country is forest, river and a long white beach, and the folk song tradition is enormous: over a million texts collected, and a festival that fills a stadium to sing them.

season.note: June and July are the point — long light, warm sea at Jūrmala, and the midsummer festivities that stop the country. Winter is grey and cheap, and Riga's covered market is at its best in it.

getting_around: Riga is compact and walkable; trains reach Jūrmala and Sigulda in under an hour and cost almost nothing. Long-distance buses beat trains for everywhere else.
food: Rye bread, and rye bread ice cream, which works
Grey peas with bacon, the national dish and unapologetically heavy
Smoked fish from the Kurzeme coast, bought at the roadside

festivals.name: Song and Dance Celebration — every five years, tens of thousands of singers
Jāņi, midsummer with wreaths and cheese

know: Riga's Central Market occupies five former Zeppelin hangars.
The Latvian language is one of only two surviving Baltic languages, and older in structure than most of Europe's.
Forest covers more than half the country and mushrooming in autumn is a national activity.

regions.name: Riga & Around
regions.summary: The capital, its Art Nouveau quarter, a beach resort down the line and a castle valley up it.

cities.name: Riga
cities.summary: A hanseatic old town wrapped in a boulevard ring, wrapped in the best Art Nouveau streets in Europe.
highlights: Alberta iela, where Mikhail Eisenstein put faces on every facade
The Central Market in five Zeppelin hangars
The wooden architecture of Kalnciema across the river
The Latvian National Museum of Art, sharp and well-lit

experiences.name: The facades of Alberta iela
experiences.summary: Ninety minutes and a raised chin: everything worth seeing here is above the first floor.

experiences.name: Lunch in the Zeppelin hangars
experiences.summary: Smoked fish, black bread, curd and pickles bought from four different counters and eaten standing up.

cities.name: Sigulda
cities.summary: Three castles above a sandstone river gorge, an hour from Riga by train.
highlights: Turaida's red brick castle above the Gauja
Gūtmanis cave, carved with visitors' names since the 1600s
The bobsleigh track, open to the public in winter

regions.name: Kurzeme & the Coast
regions.summary: The western province: empty white beaches, a Soviet ghost town, and Liepāja's wind.

cities.name: Liepāja
cities.summary: A wind-blown port with a derelict tsarist naval town at its northern end and a rock music habit.
highlights: Karosta: a Russian imperial naval base, half-ruined, still lived in
The northern forts collapsing into the sea

cities.name: Kuldīga
cities.summary: A wooden town on Europe's widest waterfall, which is only two metres high but 249 metres across.
highlights: Ventas rumba, where fish jump the falls in spring
Timber streets almost untouched since the 18th century
